sources.title: Beacon Power Services: harnessing data to drive Africa’s energy transition
sources.notes: Locators: “In Abuja, a network transitioning from ‘flying blind’ to real-time visibility” and the paragraph describing CAIMS, Adora and Xepp. Includes direct comment from an AEDC director. Proparco is a BPS investor, so reported outcomes are not imported without additional corroboration.

sources.title: Digital Energy Challenge: innovative projects paving the way for Africa’s energy transition
sources.notes: Locator: “Reducing power outages in Nigeria: AEDC x Beacon Power Services.” Supports the named partnership, Nigeria, the 2023 programme-support year and reported implementation activity. AFD administers the supporting programme; outcome figures require separate scrutiny.

sources.title: Beacon Power Services — Transforming Energy Management in Africa through Innovation
sources.notes: Locator: homepage and company footer. Used only for the provider’s current canonical website; it does not independently establish origin, headquarters or deployment.

sources.title: CAIMS — Customer and Asset Information Management System | Beacon Power Services
sources.notes: Locator: CAIMS overview, Features, Functionalities and Technical Specifications. Supports product functions as provider claims; customer outcomes are not imported from this page.

sources.title: Pai Enterprise Dashboard | PowerLabs
sources.notes: Locators: Analytics, Sizing Optimisation, Anomaly Detections and Use Cases. Supports the current product URL and provider-described functionality; it does not independently establish deployments.

sources.title: PAM AFRICA | Digital Energy Facility
sources.notes: Locators: “The Project at a Glance,” “How It Works” and “Results So Far.” Supports PAM-AI, Nigeria, KEDCO and unnamed mini-grid implementations. It is programme evidence, not customer confirmation; outcome figures are excluded.

sources.title: Adora — Grid Network Management | Beacon Power Services
sources.notes: Locator: Adora overview, Features, Functionalities and Technical Specifications. Supports product functions as provider claims; performance claims are not imported.

sources.title: This startup is building an ‘intelligence layer’ for Nigeria’s power grid
sources.notes: Locators: article introduction, “How the system works” and the Pai Enterprise launch paragraph. Independently supports company and product existence, Lagos base and June 2025 launch. Regional usage is attributed to the founder and is retained only as claimed availability, never as deployment evidence.

sources.title: Xepp — Track energy, pay for electricity and go solar | Beacon Power Services
sources.notes: Locator: Features, Functionalities and Technical Specifications. The page states that the app is available on iOS and Android and is free to download and use; product claims remain provider-authored.
